description: FUTURE SERVICE NOTE, built and held off: an outside provider publishes defined terms for an amount of computing or data capacity they say exists now, for a window that starts soon, and a buyer notes that they may want some of it. Both are records, each signed by the wallet that made it. Nothing is prepaid: no NET moves before the work is delivered, and a note reserves, holds, locks and pays nothing. Nothing here creates a prepayment, which would be a real liability. A conversion is different from a note: it takes its units off the terms' capacity while its order stands (a quote stands for up to 48 hours). The house is never the provider or the buyer. You name one act: publish_terms (a provider publishes terms: a kind of capacity and its unit, how much, a price per unit in NET units, the most one note may ask for, a delivery window and the last time a note can be signed, plus the provider's own statements capacityExistsNow true and noPaymentBeforeAcceptance true), signal_intent (a buyer notes a nonbinding interest in some units of published terms, naming the terms' id and hash and the buyer's own statement nonbinding true), convert_intent (the buyer turns their own note into an ordinary order, quoted at the provider's published price for the units noted), or withdraw (the wallet that made a record ends it, a provider ends their terms, or a provider ends a note on their terms; an order still before delivery is cancelled). The notice's version and hash (net_future_service_status gives both) are named by publish_terms and signal_intent. The statements are never assumed for you. You choose the record's id; net_future_service_status reads a record back by that id, and prepare never does, because it answers the same for every wallet. FREE to sign, no fee, no gas. An ordinary order is a DRY RUN for now: it checks no balance and no payment can be recorded for it. A provider says the capacity exists; nobody here checks it. The program is built but held off until the operator switches it on, and it stays out of the joint switch-on: until then a new record or a conversion is refused before you sign, and a withdrawal only works on a record that exists. What depends on this wallet's own records or roles is answered only when you submit, so prepare never says which wallet holds what: an id already in use, a note or terms the wallet already holds or the most it may keep, a wallet that is the provider of the terms it notes against, a conversion or a withdrawal by a wallet that did not make the record, and a note whose order is already delivered. If one applies, nothing is recorded, and a refusal made after the signature is verified also spends that signature. This moves no NET, and the house pays, holds and sells nothing through these tools. Never put a phone number, an email or a street address in any field. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with the acting wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_net_future_service within 5 minutes. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

capacityExistsNow.description: publish_terms: true is YOUR statement that this capacity exists now. Nobody checks it for you, and it is never assumed for you.

capacityUnits.description: publish_terms: how many units you say you can deliver now, a whole number up to 1,000,000.

deliveryEndsAt.description: publish_terms: when the delivery window ends, an ISO UTC time. The window runs at most 60 days.

deliveryStartsAt.description: publish_terms: when the delivery window starts, an ISO UTC time such as 2026-11-20T00:00:00Z. It must start within 14 days.

endsAt.description: publish_terms: the last time a note can be signed, an ISO UTC time not after the window ends.

maxUnitsPerIntent.description: publish_terms: the most one note may ask for, from 1 up to capacityUnits. This number times the price is at most 100,000 NET units.

noPaymentBeforeAcceptance.description: publish_terms: true is YOUR statement that you ask for and take no payment before the delivery is accepted. It is never assumed for you.

nonbinding.description: signal_intent: true is YOUR statement that this note reserves, promises and pays nothing. It is never assumed for you.

noticeSha256.description: publish_terms or signal_intent: the 64-character lowercase hash of the notice you read. A changed word changes the hash.

noticeVersion.description: publish_terms or signal_intent: the version of the notice you read (net_future_service_status gives it).

principal.description: The 0x… address that signs: the wallet that makes or ends the record. Address only, never a private key.

reason.description: withdraw: optional, one plain sentence, up to 280 characters. Only you ever read it back.

recordId.description: The record's id: 1 to 80 letters, numbers and . _ : -. You choose it when you publish or note; for convert_intent it is your note's id, and for withdraw the id of the record to end. net_future_service_status reads a record back by its id.

termsId.description: signal_intent: the id of the published terms (net_future_service_status lists them).

termsSha256.description: signal_intent: the 64-character lowercase hash of the terms you read, exactly as the read gave it.

unitLabel.description: publish_terms: the unit. compute takes cpu_hours, gpu_hours or job_runs; data takes records, queries or gigabytes.

unitPriceNetUnits.description: publish_terms: your price for one unit, a whole number of NET units, at least 1 (1 NET is 1,000,000 units).

units.description: signal_intent: how many units you may want, a whole number. It is your own number, never filled in for you.

name: prepare_net_future_service
title: Publish terms, note a nonbinding interest, convert your own note, or withdraw a record: the future service note (step 1 of 2)
